name: graph-derived-output-disclosure-selection
originalRequirement: Controlled cross-format conversions must disclose source, target path, overwrite strategy and conversion loss, keep the source safe, and automatically open the created target.

candidates.source: the selected top-level graph object and its 1-to-4-level local graph
candidates.target: a new numbered Canvas in the library root
derivedFacts: all included graph nodes become relative file nodes
included relations retain direction and relation type
positions are regenerated by breadth-first depth rather than preserving graph layout
the Canvas is an independent point-in-time relationship snapshot
candidates.currentGap: There is no pre-write disclosure, and the frontend enables the action for every top-level object while the local-graph backend currently accepts only Markdown or PDF centers.

candidates.source: the selected top-level Markdown or PDF graph object and its 1-to-4-level local graph
candidates.target: a new numbered Markdown file beside the center object
derivedFacts: a generated metadata header records the center and clamped depth
a fixed goal and next-step task template is inserted
related objects are sorted by title and path
at most 100 related objects are written and any omitted count is disclosed inside the note
the note is an independently editable point-in-time derivative
candidates.currentGap: There is no pre-write disclosure; frontend and backend eligibility, numbered new-file behavior and automatic opening are otherwise aligned.

selection.name: graph-project-note-disclosure
selection.reason: The project-note path has a coherent Markdown/PDF eligibility boundary and can close the original disclosure requirement without first changing graph object eligibility. Graph-to-Canvas must first reconcile its frontend/backend center-type drift and remains a separate later batch.
